keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Zazzau row). "Zazzau is thought to have been founded in or about 1536"; Amina's campaigns "made the kingdoms of Kano and Katsina tributary" and between the 15th and 16th centuries Zazzau was a tributary of Songhai, after Amina's death under Jukun influence. The page names only the four Kaduna State local-government areas (Zaria, Sabon Gari, Giwa, Soba) and gives no outline, so Kaduna stands for the kingdom at confidence 1.

ledger.note: About 1536: Zazzau is founded. "Zazzau is thought to have been founded in or about 1536"; the page adds that the city was renamed in the late 16th century after Queen Amina's sister, Zaria. (A "tributary state of the Songhai Empire between the fifteenth and sixteenth century" does not fit the date.)

notes:
Zazzau (Zaria), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Zazzau, Fulani War.

The Zazzau page is about the city and emirate; it has no infobox dates, no capital moves (Turunku, Kwatarkwashi, Abuja are named elsewhere), no Amina reign dates, no Bornu relation. It gives 1805 for the Fulani capture (Fulani War page silent), 1901 for the British (Lugard, no month). The founding "in or about 1536" sits oddly with a Songhai tribute in "the fifteenth and sixteenth century" and with Amina's late-16th-century conquests; kept as the page's only date. The emirate, a Sokoto subdivision, is not drawn here. The Kaduna region is far larger than the four local-government areas the page names.
